Package br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.domain.capture

Class StreamCamera

java.lang.Object
br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.domain.capture.Camera
br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.domain.capture.StreamCamera
public final class StreamCamera extends Camera
A camera that is not mounted on the court but streams to it over the network — a phone on a tripod.

The only kind whose clip is a real file: it hands its window to an assembler that writes the video, where the other kinds only name a file that nothing writes.

    • StreamCamera

      public StreamCamera(String id, String model, Resolution resolution, int bufferSeconds, String streamUrl, ClipAssembler assembler)
      Builds a stream camera, switched off. Building it opens no connection: the address is only recorded here.
      Parameters:
      id - the identifier, unique across the gym the camera is installed in
      model - the make and model of the phone or device
      resolution - the resolution it streams at
      bufferSeconds - how many of the most recent seconds the camera keeps
      streamUrl - the address the device streams from
      assembler - what writes this camera's clips to disk
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the id, model or stream address is missing or blank, the resolution or assembler is missing, or the buffer is not at least one second long

  • Method Details

    • captureLastSeconds

      public VideoClip captureLastSeconds(int seconds)
      Freezes the most recent seconds into a clip. Each kind of camera produces one its own way, and a court triggers them all through this single call.

      Every kind keeps one promise: the clip is finished when this returns. A kind that writes a file has written it, so whoever holds the clip may archive it at once, without knowing which kind of camera cut it.

      The file is written before this returns: the camera waits for its assembler however long the write takes, and never hands back a clip whose file is still to come.

      Specified by:
      captureLastSeconds in class Camera
      Parameters:
      seconds - how much of the recent past to keep
      Returns:
      the finished clip that stands for those seconds
      Throws:
      ClipAssemblyException - if the file could not be written
